c.name: C
c.blurb: The language under almost everything, including Genesis games written with SGDK. The best place to start.

lessons.title: Hello, World
goals: Know what a program, a compiler, and running are
Write and run a program that prints a message with printf
Use \n to start a new line

lessons.title: Comments and Mistakes
goals: Write // and /* */ comments
Read a compiler error and find the line it points to
Tell errors and warnings apart, and fix both

lessons.title: Variables and Types
goals: Declare and assign int, char, and double variables
Print values with %d, %c, and %f
Explain what a type is and why C needs it

lessons.title: Math and Operators
goals: Use + - * / and %
Predict integer division and remainder results
Use ++, --, += and operator precedence

lessons.title: Reading Input
goals: Read numbers with scanf and the & sign
Type input into the terminal while a program runs
Build a tiny calculator

lessons.title: Decisions: if and else
goals: Compare values with == != < > <= >=
Combine conditions with && || !
Know that 0 means false and anything else means true

lessons.title: Loops: while and for
goals: Repeat code with while and for
Trace a loop by hand, step by step
Stop a stuck infinite loop and understand why it happened

lessons.title: switch, break and continue
goals: Choose between cases with switch
Leave or skip loop steps with break and continue
Write a menu-driven program

lessons.title: Functions
goals: Define and call functions with parameters and return values
Explain local scope
Declare a function before it's used (prototypes)

lessons.title: Arrays
goals: Create arrays and index them from 0
Loop over an array
Recognize an out-of-bounds bug and the error it causes

lessons.title: Characters and Strings
goals: Store text in char arrays
Explain the '\0' terminator
Use strlen, strcpy, and strcmp safely

lessons.title: Binary, Hex and Bits
goals: Convert between decimal, binary, and hexadecimal
Use & | ^ ~ << >> on numbers
Pack on/off flags into one number with masks

lessons.title: Memory and Addresses
goals: Picture memory as numbered boxes
Get an address with & and a size with sizeof
Explain how a variable is laid out in bytes

lessons.title: Pointers
goals: Declare a pointer and dereference it with *
Walk through an array with a pointer
Explain NULL and why using it crashes

lessons.title: Pointers and Functions
goals: Let a function change a variable through a pointer
Write a swap function
Use const to promise not to change data

lessons.title: Structs
goals: Group related data into a struct
Use . and -> to reach fields
Keep an array of game objects

lessons.title: Exact-size Integers and Overflow
goals: Use uint8_t, int16_t, uint32_t from stdint.h
Predict what happens when a number overflows
Choose signed or unsigned deliberately

lessons.title: Dynamic Memory
goals: Allocate and free memory with malloc and free
Recognize leaks and use-after-free bugs
Understand why console games avoid malloc

lessons.title: Multiple Files and Headers
goals: Split code into .c and .h files
Use #include, #define, and include guards
Explain what the compiler and linker each do

lessons.title: Project: A Game Loop
goals: Plan a small terminal game before coding it
Combine structs, loops, functions, and input
Debug it by reading output and errors

cpp.name: C++
cpp.blurb: C plus classes, strings, and a big standard library. Used for most modern games and tools.

lessons.title: Hello, C++
goals: Print with std::cout and read with std::cin
Explain namespaces and std::
Know what C++ adds to C

lessons.title: Variables, auto and References
goals: Use auto sensibly
Create references and compare them to pointers
Use const everywhere it fits

lessons.title: std::string
goals: Build, join, and compare strings
Read a whole line with std::getline
Explain why std::string is safer than char arrays

lessons.title: std::vector
goals: Store a growing list in a vector
Loop over it with range-for
Add, remove, and look up items

lessons.title: Functions, Overloads and Defaults
goals: Overload a function by parameter types
Use default arguments
Pass by value, by reference, and by const reference

lessons.title: Classes and Objects
goals: Write a class with data and methods
Use public and private
Explain what an object is

lessons.title: Constructors and Destructors
goals: Initialize objects with constructors
Clean up in destructors
Explain RAII and why it prevents leaks

lessons.title: Operator Overloading
goals: Write a Vec2 type with + and * operators
Print your own types with <<
Know when operator overloading helps or hurts

lessons.title: Inheritance and Virtual Functions
goals: Derive classes from a base class
Override virtual functions
Store different game entities in one list

lessons.title: Smart Pointers
goals: Own objects with std::unique_ptr
Share them with std::shared_ptr
Explain ownership

lessons.title: Templates
goals: Write a template function
Write a simple template class
Read template error messages

lessons.title: Algorithms and Lambdas
goals: Sort and search with <algorithm>
Write lambdas
Pick the right algorithm instead of writing loops

lessons.title: Maps and Sets
goals: Look up values by key with std::map and std::unordered_map
Keep unique items in a set
Choose a container for a job

lessons.title: Errors and Exceptions
goals: Throw and catch exceptions
Use return values or std::optional instead when better
Know why games often turn exceptions off

lessons.title: Organizing a Project
goals: Split classes into headers and source files
Use namespaces for your own code
Keep a project easy to read

lessons.title: Project: A Tiny Game Engine
goals: Design entities with update and draw steps
Run them in a fixed-step game loop
Extend it with a new entity type

sgdk.name: SGDK: C on the Genesis
sgdk.blurb: Make real Sega Genesis games in C with SGDK. The fastest way to see your own game on a Genesis.

lessons.title: What SGDK Is
goals: Explain how C becomes a Genesis ROM
Know what SGDK gives you and what it hides
Show text on screen with VDP_drawText

lessons.title: The Main Loop and VBlank
goals: Explain frames and vertical blank (60 Hz NTSC / 50 Hz PAL)
Write a main loop with SYS_doVBlankProcess
Count frames on screen

lessons.title: Tiles and Palettes
goals: Explain 8×8 tiles and 4-bit color
Explain the 4 palettes of 16 colors
Change colors with PAL_setColor

lessons.title: Backgrounds and Planes
goals: Explain planes A and B and the window
Import an image with rescomp
Draw a background on a plane

lessons.title: Reading the Controller
goals: Read buttons with JOY_readJoypad
Use a joypad event handler
Tell 'held' from 'just pressed'

lessons.title: Sprites
goals: Import a sprite sheet
Show and animate a sprite with the SPR engine
Know the hardware sprite limits

lessons.title: Moving a Character
goals: Move with position and velocity
Use fixed-point numbers (fix16) instead of floats
Add gravity and jumping

lessons.title: Scrolling
goals: Scroll a plane horizontally and vertically
Make parallax with two planes
Follow the player with a camera

lessons.title: Collision
goals: Check box-against-box collision
Collide with a tile map
Respond to collisions without getting stuck

lessons.title: Sound and Music
goals: Play music with XGM
Play sound effects
Know what the Z80 and YM2612 do

lessons.title: Game States
goals: Switch between title, game, and game over screens
Reset cleanly between states
Keep state code organized

lessons.title: Maps with Tiled
goals: Draw a level in Tiled
Load it with rescomp
Scroll through a large map

lessons.title: Speed on a 7.6 MHz CPU
goals: Measure how long a frame's work takes
Avoid division, floats, and wasted work
Use DMA well

lessons.title: Looking Under the Hood
goals: Read the 68000 assembly your C turns into
Connect C statements to instructions
Spot slow code by reading assembly

lessons.title: Mixing C and Assembly
goals: Call an assembly routine from C
Pass arguments between them
Decide when assembly is worth it

lessons.title: Project: A Small Genesis Game
goals: Plan a one-screen game
Build it with sprites, input, collision, and sound
Test it on an accurate emulator

m68k.name: 68000 Assembly (Sega Genesis)
m68k.blurb: Talk to the Genesis directly in the language its games were written in. The path to homebrew and Sonic hacking.

lessons.title: How a Computer Runs Code
goals: Picture the CPU, memory, and instructions
Explain what assembly and an assembler are
Know how source code becomes a ROM that runs

lessons.title: Binary and Hexadecimal
goals: Count in binary and hex ($ and % notation)
Read hex as shorthand for groups of 4 bits
Know bits, nybbles, bytes, words, and longwords

lessons.title: Memory and Addresses
goals: Picture memory as numbered bytes
Explain big-endian byte order
Know the Genesis memory map in outline (ROM, RAM at $FF0000, hardware)

lessons.title: Registers
goals: Name D0–D7, A0–A7, PC and SR
Know that A7 is the stack pointer
Know what each kind of register is for

lessons.title: move and Sizes
goals: Use move.b, move.w and move.l
Tell #immediate numbers from memory addresses
Predict what a byte or word write leaves in a register

lessons.title: Addressing Modes I
goals: Use Dn, An, #imm, absolute and (An)
Load addresses with lea
Read a value from a table

lessons.title: Addressing Modes II
goals: Use (An)+, -(An), d(An) and d(An,Xn)
Use PC-relative addressing
Walk through a list of records

lessons.title: Arithmetic
goals: Use add, sub, addq, subq, addi, neg
Use ext, clr, swap and exg
Know when a quick form (addq, moveq) applies

lessons.title: The Condition Codes
goals: Explain the X N Z V C flags
Know which instructions set them
Use tst and cmp

lessons.title: Branching
goals: Branch with bra and Bcc
Choose signed (bgt, blt) vs unsigned (bhi, bcs) branches
Turn an if/else into assembly

lessons.title: Loops with dbra
goals: Write counting loops with dbra
Explain why you load the count minus one
Loop over a table and sum it

lessons.title: Bits and Shifts
goals: Use and, or, eor, not, btst, bset, bclr
Shift and rotate with lsl, lsr, asl, asr, rol
Multiply and divide by powers of two with shifts

lessons.title: Multiply and Divide
goals: Use mulu, muls, divu, divs and their sizes
Know what they cost in cycles
Avoid them where speed matters

lessons.title: Subroutines and the Stack
goals: Call code with bsr/jsr and return with rts
Push and pop with the stack pointer
Save and restore registers with movem

lessons.title: Directives, Data and Tables
goals: Use labels, equ, dc.b/dc.w/dc.l and even
Lay out records with offsets
Use lookup tables and jump tables

lessons.title: Anatomy of a Genesis ROM
goals: Lay out the vector table and ROM header
Explain TMSS and the 'SEGA' handshake
Know which header fields the console checks

lessons.title: Booting the Genesis
goals: Write the startup code step by step
Explain each step instead of copying it
Know what emulators forgive that real hardware doesn't

lessons.title: Talking to the VDP
goals: Use the VDP control and data ports
Set VDP registers
Build VRAM, CRAM, and VSRAM command words

lessons.title: Colors and Palettes
goals: Encode a color in CRAM format
Load a 16-color palette
Turn the whole screen a color

lessons.title: Tiles, Planes and Hello World
goals: Draw an 8×8 tile in 4-bit pixels
Explain planes and nametable entries
Load a font and print 'Hello World'

lessons.title: Sprites
goals: Fill in the sprite attribute table
Use size bits and the link field
Show a sprite

lessons.title: VBlank and the Game Loop
goals: Set up a vertical blank interrupt
Wait for VBlank in the main loop
Know what work belongs in VBlank

lessons.title: Reading the Controller
goals: Read a 3-button pad through the I/O ports
Tell held from just pressed
Move a sprite with the D-pad

lessons.title: DMA and Animation
goals: Copy to VRAM with DMA
Know when DMA is safe and how much fits in a frame
Animate a sprite

lessons.title: Scrolling
goals: Scroll planes with the H-scroll table and VSRAM
Use full, cell, and line scroll modes
Make a scrolling starfield

lessons.title: Sound Basics
goals: Make tones and noise with the PSG
Request and release the Z80 bus
Know what sound drivers do and which you may use

lessons.title: Game Structure
goals: Store objects as fixed-size records in RAM
Run each object's code every frame with a state machine
Check collisions and make pseudo-random numbers

lessons.title: Project: Pong in Assembly
goals: Plan Pong before coding it
Build it with sprites, input, collision and sound
Compare it with a version written in C

sonic.name: Sonic ROM Hacking
sonic.blurb: Take apart the Sonic disassemblies and change them properly, understanding every edit.

lessons.title: ROMs and Disassemblies
goals: Explain what a disassembly is
Know why hackers edit source instead of ROMs
Know the Sonic 1, 2 and 3&K repositories

lessons.title: Setting Up
goals: Clone a disassembly and build it
Check the build matches the original ROM exactly
Run it in an emulator with a debugger

lessons.title: Git Habits
goals: Commit before every change
Read a diff and undo a change
Find the change that broke a build

lessons.title: Touring the Code
goals: Read the folder layout and main source file
Follow the main loop and game modes
Search for a label and follow it

lessons.title: First Edits
goals: Change starting rings and lives
Change a speed constant and predict the result
Rebuild and test every time

lessons.title: The RAM Map
goals: Find the player's object fields
Find important global variables
Watch RAM change in a debugger

lessons.title: Palettes
goals: Find and edit palette data
Explain palette cycling
Change a zone's colors

lessons.title: Art and Mappings
goals: Explain Nemesis and Kosinski compression
Explain sprite mappings and DPLCs
Edit art with Flex 2 or ClownMapEd

lessons.title: Levels
goals: Explain chunks, blocks and layouts
Edit a level with SonLVL
Explain where collision data lives

lessons.title: Objects
goals: Explain object slots and status table fields
Follow an object's routine counter
Change a badnik's behavior

lessons.title: Player Physics
goals: Read Sonic's movement code alongside the Sonic Physics Guide
Explain sensors, slopes and jumping
Change jump height properly

lessons.title: Following a Guide Critically
goals: Apply a guide (like the Sonic 1 Spin Dash) to the right disassembly version
Understand every line you add
Spot the limitations a guide introduces

lessons.title: Debugging Crashes
goals: Install an error handler
Read an exception screen
Trace a crash back to its cause

lessons.title: Fixing Bugs Properly
goals: Apply common Sonic 1/2 bug fixes
Explain why each bug happened
Know branch-range, alignment and RAM-limit errors

lessons.title: A New Ability or Object
goals: Design something small (for example an air dash)
Give it art, mappings and code
Fit it into object RAM and VRAM safely

lessons.title: Sound and Shipping
goals: Explain what SMPS is and its limits
Make a patch file (BPS/IPS) for release
Test on accurate emulators and write release notes

nes.name: 6502 Assembly (NES)
nes.blurb: Program the Nintendo Entertainment System in 6502 assembly: tiles, sprites, the controller and sound, ending with a tiny game.

lessons.title: How the NES Runs a Game
goals: Picture the NES's parts: the CPU (a 6502 inside the Ricoh 2A03), the PPU that draws the picture, RAM, and the cartridge
Know what PRG ROM (code) and CHR ROM (graphics) are
Explain what assembly, an assembler and a linker do

lessons.title: Binary, Hex and Bytes
goals: Count in binary and hex and read $ and % notation
Know that the 6502 works in bytes and that addresses are 16 bits
Read a byte as unsigned (0–255) or signed (−128 to 127)

lessons.title: Registers and Your First Instructions
goals: Know the A, X and Y registers and what each is for
Use LDA, LDX, LDY, STA, STX and STY
Tell immediate (#) values from memory addresses

lessons.title: The Toolchain: ca65 and ld65
goals: Know what segments are and why NES programs use them
Write an iNES header and explain each byte
Read a linker config for an NROM cartridge and know how a .nes file gets built

lessons.title: The NES Memory Map
goals: Know where RAM, the zero page and the stack live
Find the PPU registers ($2000–$2007) and the APU and controller registers ($4000s)
Explain the reset, NMI and IRQ vectors at $FFFA–$FFFF

lessons.title: Flags and Arithmetic
goals: Know the N, V, Z and C flags and which instructions change them
Add and subtract with ADC and SBC, using CLC and SEC correctly
Use INC, DEC, INX, INY, DEX and DEY

lessons.title: Comparing and Branching
goals: Compare with CMP, CPX and CPY and read the result from the flags
Branch with BEQ, BNE, BCC, BCS, BMI and BPL
Write a counting loop and know a branch's −128 to +127 byte range

lessons.title: Addressing Modes
goals: Use zero page and absolute addressing and know why zero page is faster
Step through tables with indexed modes (,X and ,Y)
Use pointers with indirect indexed addressing: (zp),Y

lessons.title: Subroutines and the Stack
goals: Call and return with JSR and RTS
Save and restore registers with PHA, PLA, PHP and PLP
Explain what the stack page ($0100–$01FF) holds and why it must balance

lessons.title: Bits and Logic
goals: Mask and combine bits with AND, ORA and EOR
Shift and rotate with ASL, LSR, ROL and ROR
Test bits with BIT and know why the NES uses bit flags everywhere

lessons.title: Booting the NES
goals: Write a reset handler: interrupts off, stack set, PPU and APU quiet
Wait for the PPU to warm up with two vblank waits
Clear RAM and explain why each step is needed

lessons.title: How the PPU Draws Tiles
goals: Know pattern tables, 8×8 tiles and the 2-bit-per-pixel CHR format
Use PPUCTRL, PPUMASK and PPUSTATUS
Write to PPU memory through PPUADDR and PPUDATA, and reset the address latch

lessons.title: Palettes and Color
goals: Know the NES palette and the 32 bytes of palette memory at $3F00
Load background and sprite palettes
Turn rendering on and see your first colors

lessons.title: Backgrounds: Nametables
goals: Know the 32×30 nametable and its address math
Use attribute tables to pick palettes for 16×16 areas
Draw a screen of tiles and a line of text

lessons.title: Vblank and the NMI
goals: Explain vertical blank and why the PPU is only safe to change then
Write an NMI handler and enable NMIs in PPUCTRL
Build a once-per-frame main loop and reset the scroll

lessons.title: Sprites
goals: Know OAM and the 4 bytes of a sprite (Y, tile, attributes, X)
Keep a shadow copy of OAM in RAM and send it with OAM DMA ($4014)
Show, hide and flip sprites and know the 8-sprites-per-line limit

lessons.title: Reading the Controller
goals: Strobe and read the controller through $4016
Pack the 8 buttons into one byte
Detect new presses versus held buttons

lessons.title: Moving a Character
goals: Move a sprite with the D-pad, once per frame
Keep it on the screen
Organize the game loop: read input, update, then let the NMI draw

lessons.title: Metasprites and Animation
goals: Build a character from several sprites with a metasprite table
Animate with a frame counter and a table of frames
Flip a metasprite to face left and right

lessons.title: Collisions
goals: Check two boxes for overlap with comparisons
Handle 8-bit wraparound safely
React to a hit: score, sound or reset

lessons.title: Scrolling
goals: Use PPUSCROLL and the nametable bits in PPUCTRL
Know vertical and horizontal mirroring and what the iNES header sets
Scroll a background smoothly

lessons.title: Sound with the APU
goals: Know the APU's channels: two pulses, triangle, noise and DMC
Play a tone on a pulse channel and pick its pitch
Make a short sound effect that plays over several frames

lessons.title: Organizing a Bigger Program
goals: Use constants, zero-page variables, .proc scopes and include files
Write a macro and know when a subroutine is better
Lay out a project so it stays readable

lessons.title: Your First NES Game
goals: Combine everything into a tiny complete game
Review what was built and why each part works
Know the next steps: mappers, music engines, more tools
